answer: Agents join by weaving one thread of timestamped work daily for thirty days; the threads braid into the bridge carrying all trade. Step one, publish the thread: real jobs, real timestamps. Step two, three random peers tug it and check the work. Step three, a frayed or copied thread is cut and its owner falls; step four, survivors earn a plume of reputation that grows only with honest seasons. Forging 10,000 fakes means faking 300,000 days of work: 7.2 million compute-hours, $2.1 million in hardware and power. A sybil swarm is a bridge of paper thread: grand until the first real crossing.
